mechanism: Erenumab-aooe is a human monoclonal antibody that binds to the calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor and antagonizes CGRP receptor function.
phase: Phase 3 pediatric label-expansion study; marketed/approved adult product
development_status: ClinicalTrials.gov lists OASIS PEDIATRIC (EM), NCT03836040, as an active, not recruiting Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in children 6 to <12 years and adolescents 12 to <18 years with episodic migraine. Actual enrollment is 457, actual primary completion was November 19, 2025, estimated study completion is November 15, 2026, and no ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted. Aimovig is already FDA-approved and marketed for preventive treatment of migraine in adults, but current U.S. labeling states it is not known if Aimovig is safe and effective in children under 18 years of age.
expected_launch_window: 2027-2028 pediatric label-expansion window if Phase 3 data support filing; adult migraine product already launched in 2018
clinical_summary: NCT03836040 is testing once-monthly subcutaneous erenumab dose levels by body weight versus placebo for pediatric episodic migraine, with primary efficacy based on change from baseline in monthly migraine days at weeks 9 through 12. No Phase 3 pediatric efficacy results are posted yet. A prior Phase 1 pediatric study of 53 children and adolescents found erenumab exposures increased approximately dose-proportionally and the observed pediatric PK and safety profile were consistent with adults when body-weight differences were considered. Adult Aimovig efficacy and long market experience support biologic plausibility, but differentiation for pediatrics is limited because Ajovy received FDA pediatric episodic migraine approval in August 2025 and NCT03836040 has not yet reported efficacy results.
safety_summary: Current Aimovig labeling warns about serious hypersensitivity, constipation with serious complications, new-onset or worsening hypertension, and Raynaud's phenomenon; common adverse reactions in adult clinical studies were injection-site reactions and constipation. The pediatric Phase 1 study reported TEAEs in 42 of 53 participants (79.2%) and serious TEAEs in 4 participants (7.5%), none considered treatment-related; common TEAEs were upper respiratory tract infection, headache, and vomiting, with no clinically significant vital-sign, ECG, laboratory, or neurologic changes. NCT03836040 includes pediatric safety, growth/development, bone-marker, immunogenicity, and suicidality measures through up to 80 weeks, but results are not posted.
management_tools: Flag as a marketed adult product and pediatric label-expansion study rather than a novel molecular pipeline launch
Age and indication edit aligned to any final pediatric label if approved
Document baseline monthly migraine or headache days before authorization
Continuation criteria requiring documented clinical benefit, such as reduced migraine days or reduced severe migraine days
Quantity limit of one 70 mg/mL or 140 mg/mL autoinjector per 30 days unless final pediatric dosing requires a different presentation
Concurrent-use edit against another preventive CGRP inhibitor, including preventive rimegepant use where policy permits
Preferred-product or step-through positioning versus currently pediatric-approved Ajovy if formulary strategy requires differentiation
evidence_gaps: No posted ClinicalTrials.gov results for NCT03836040 despite actual primary completion on 2025-11-19.
No public Amgen pediatric filing, approval date, or top-line Phase 3 OASIS PEDIATRIC (EM) efficacy release was found.
Dose 1 is not numerically disclosed in the ClinicalTrials.gov intervention field; dosing is described as body-weight based.
Annual cost uses current adult Aimovig WAC for 70 mg and 140 mg monthly products as the closest public price analog; final pediatric pricing or presentation may differ.
Pediatric competitive context changed because Ajovy became FDA-approved for episodic migraine prevention in patients aged 6 to 17 years weighing at least 45 kg in August 2025.

sources.title: Efficacy and Safety of Erenumab in Pediatric Participants With Episodic Migraine
supports: Official title is a Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study of erenumab in children 6 to <12 years and adolescents 12 to <18 years with episodic migraine.
Sponsor is Amgen and collaborator is Novartis.
Overall status is active, not recruiting; actual enrollment is 457; actual start was 2019-07-19; actual primary completion was 2025-11-19; estimated completion is 2026-11-15.
Interventions include Erenumab Dose 1, Dose 2, Dose 3, and placebo; Dose 1 is for participants in the low body-weight group randomized to Dose Level 1.
Primary outcome is change from baseline in monthly migraine days from baseline to weeks 9 through 12 of the double-blind treatment phase.

Secondary and safety outcomes include 50% monthly migraine day response, headache days, PedMIDAS disability, TEAEs, bone markers, anti-erenumab antibodies, growth and development, and C-SSRS measures.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

sources.title: DailyMed: AIMOVIG (erenumab-aooe) injection, solution
supports: Aimovig is indicated for the preventive treatment of migraine in adults.
Recommended adult dose is 70 mg once monthly; some patients may benefit from 140 mg once monthly.
Available strengths are 70 mg/mL and 140 mg/mL single-dose prefilled SureClick autoinjectors and syringes.
Mechanism of action is binding to the CGRP receptor and antagonizing CGRP receptor function.
Warnings include hypersensitivity, constipation with serious complications, hypertension, and Raynaud's phenomenon.
Common adverse reactions in adult clinical studies were injection-site reactions and constipation.
Patient labeling states it is not known if Aimovig is safe and effective in children under 18 years of age.

sources.title: FDA Approves Aimovig (erenumab-aooe), A Novel Treatment Developed Specifically For Migraine Prevention
supports: Amgen announced FDA approval of Aimovig for preventive treatment of migraine in adults on 2018-05-17.
Aimovig was described as a CGRP receptor blocker and once-monthly self-administered injection.
Amgen stated Aimovig 70 mg is self-administered once monthly and some patients may benefit from 140 mg once monthly.
The Amgen-Novartis migraine collaboration covered development and commercialization of Aimovig.

Aimovig 140 mg/mL single-dose prefilled SureClick autoinjector current WAC is $783.02 per syringe.
The WAC list price does not reflect rebates or discounts and may differ from amounts paid by providers or patients.

sources.title: Pharmacokinetics and safety of erenumab in pediatric patients with migraine: A phase I, randomized, open-label, multiple-dose study
supports: Phase 1 pediatric study evaluated safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of erenumab in children and adolescents with migraine.
Participants received erenumab 35 mg, 70 mg, or 140 mg every 4 weeks; 53 participants were treated.
Forty-eight of 53 participants completed the initial treatment phase and 36 received erenumab during extension.
Forty-two participants (79.2%) reported TEAEs and four (7.5%) reported serious TEAEs not considered treatment-related.
Common TEAEs were upper respiratory tract infection, headache, and vomiting.
The authors concluded pediatric PK and safety were consistent with adult findings when body-weight differences were considered.

sources.title: Migraine - Calcitonin Gene-Related Peptide Inhibitors - Aimovig Drug Coverage Policy
supports: Cigna requires prior authorization for prescription benefit coverage of Aimovig.

Coverage for FDA-approved migraine headache prevention requires age at least 18 years, at least 4 migraine headache days per month before migraine-preventive medication, and documented significant clinical benefit for current users.
Significant clinical benefit examples include reduction in overall migraine days per month or reduction in severe migraine days per month.

Aimovig for any other use is considered not medically necessary, including acute migraine treatment, cluster headache, concurrent use with another preventive CGRP inhibitor, preventive Nurtec ODT use, and hemiplegic migraine.
Cigna cites the 2024 American Headache Society position that CGRP-targeting therapies should be considered first-line for migraine prevention without a prior-failure requirement.

sources.title: Calcitonin Gene-Related Peptide Inhibitors - Aimovig Drug Quantity Management Policy - Per Days
supports: Drug quantity management limit is one 70 mg/mL prefilled autoinjector per 30 days at retail and three per 90 days by home delivery.
Drug quantity management limit is one 140 mg/mL prefilled autoinjector per 30 days at retail and three per 90 days by home delivery.
The policy is designed to manage potential dose escalation of Aimovig.

sources.title: DailyMed: AJOVY (fremanezumab-vfrm) injection
supports: Ajovy is indicated for preventive treatment of migraine in adults and preventive treatment of episodic migraine in pediatric patients 6 to 17 years of age who weigh 45 kg or more.
Pediatric recommended dosage is 225 mg monthly.
Ajovy is not approved in pediatric patients weighing less than 45 kg because of the lack of an appropriate strength presentation.
Recent major changes added pediatric indication and dosing in August 2025.

sources.title: AJOVY Significantly Reduced Monthly Migraine and Headache Days in Children and Adolescents with Episodic Migraine Compared to Placebo in the SPACE Trial; Results Published in New England Journal of Medicine
supports: Teva stated FDA approved Ajovy in August 2025 for preventive treatment of episodic migraine in children and adolescents aged 6 to 17 years weighing at least 45 kg.
Teva described Ajovy as the first and only CGRP antagonist indicated for both pediatric episodic migraine prevention and adult migraine prevention at that time.
SPACE trial results showed monthly migraine day reduction of 2.5 days with Ajovy versus 1.4 days with placebo and 50% responder rates of 47.2% versus 27.0%.

expected_launch_window.value: 2027-2028 pediatric label-expansion window if Phase 3 data support filing; adult migraine product already launched in 2018
expected_launch_window.method: Used the actual Phase 3 pediatric primary completion date, estimated final completion date, absence of posted results, and typical post-primary-completion filing/review timing for a marketed biologic label expansion.
expected_launch_window.explanation: The adult Aimovig product is already marketed, so the only plausible pipeline event is a pediatric episodic migraine label expansion after Phase 3 data maturity and regulatory review.

annual_cost_range.method: Applied current Aimovig WAC of $783.02 per monthly 70 mg or 140 mg autoinjector to 12 monthly fills: $783.02 x 12 = $9,396.24, rounded to $9,396.
annual_cost_range.explanation: Because Dose 1 is not numerically disclosed and pediatric pricing is not available, the estimate uses marketed adult Aimovig WAC as the closest source-backed analog and excludes rebates, discounts, patient assistance, pharmacy fees, office visits, and monitoring costs.

clinical_differentiation.method: Balanced established adult CGRP-receptor mechanism and supportive pediatric Phase 1 PK/safety against missing Phase 3 pediatric efficacy results and an already-approved pediatric CGRP competitor.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: Erenumab could add another targeted pediatric preventive option if positive, but current evidence does not show pediatric efficacy and Ajovy has already established the pediatric CGRP class entry.

budget_impact.method: Assessed monthly chronic preventive use, annual gross WAC near $9.4k, smaller pediatric episodic migraine population than adult migraine, existing specialty-drug management infrastructure, and likely pharmacy-benefit routing.
budget_impact.explanation: A pediatric expansion could increase eligible lives and family demand, but cost and controls are familiar because Aimovig is already managed in adults and a pediatric CGRP comparator is already on market.

disruption_risk.method: Rated from potential pediatric label expansion after actual primary completion, existing adult product availability, current PA/quantity controls, and the presence of pediatric-approved Ajovy.
disruption_risk.explanation: The main operational risk is policy and formulary update work for pediatric age criteria and competitor positioning, not a new-product launch build from scratch.

recommended_action.method: Recommended action reflects actual pediatric Phase 3 primary completion, expected pediatric label-expansion timing, absence of posted data, existing adult controls, and pediatric CGRP competitor approval.
recommended_action.explanation: Prepare draft pediatric criteria, age/weight edits, quantity limits, and preferred-product logic, but wait for OASIS PEDIATRIC results or FDA action before active formulary implementation.

quality_flags: Marketed/approved product study: Aimovig (erenumab-aooe) was FDA-approved for preventive treatment of migraine in adults on 2018-05-17, so NCT03836040 should not be treated as a novel molecular pipeline asset.

Pediatric label-expansion distinction: current U.S. Aimovig labeling is adult-only and states it is not known if Aimovig is safe and effective in children under 18 years of age; NCT03836040 evaluates pediatric episodic migraine.
ClinicalTrials.gov has no posted results for NCT03836040 despite actual primary completion on 2025-11-19.
Erenumab Dose 1 is a body-weight-based trial dose name; the specific milligram dose is not disclosed in the public ClinicalTrials.gov intervention description.
Annual cost estimate is gross WAC-derived from marketed adult Aimovig presentations and does not represent net payer cost or final pediatric pricing.
Pediatric CGRP competitive benchmark is already established by Ajovy's August 2025 FDA pediatric episodic migraine indication for patients aged 6 to 17 years weighing at least 45 kg.
